analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds a description around head lines 1293-1298 of PromptPieceTokenStore.lookup. The new text says lookup snapshots all of a request's hits before promoting them between two bounded generations, so a promotion that rotates the cache cannot turn a later piece into a miss. Token arrays share storage during the snapshot, existing admission and byte bounds still apply, and batches with no old-generation hits skip the promotion pass. The supplied units (base lines 2429-2954) are unchanged surrounding text from the same file. They cover MiMo ingress, Flint, tool constraints and the invariants list, and none of it is touched by the patch. No code, config, or trust-boundary behavior changes in the supplied evidence.

Threat relevance: the prompt-piece token cache is reused 'in the same prefix-cache scope'. It is adjacent to T-041 (cross-tenant prefix-cache sharing and timing). The doc states that scope is preserved and that bounds are unchanged. The PR does not alter the scoping rule, the TTL, or the at-rest crypto described in T-041.

Limit: the actual source change implementing the snapshot behavior (PromptPieceTokenStore) is not in the supplied units. I cannot verify that the code keeps scope isolation, that the generation rotation preserves the byte bounds, or that shared array storage cannot leak across scopes. This is documentation-only, so no finding qualifies. A later pass on the source change should confirm that the cache key still includes the coordinator-authored cacheSalt scope and that the bounded generations are not widened.
